channel.title: frugal blog
channel.description: Provider routing, AI tool-call costs, model selection, and agent infrastructure. By Brian Sparker.

item.title: Anatomy of a deep research agent
item.description: Log a research run and a shape appears: one plan, a burst of searches, a train of extractions, one long synthesis. Each phase costs differently. Route accordingly.

item.title: The hidden cost of retries
item.description: Every retry is a repurchase at full price with worse odds than the first attempt. Here's the playbook: budgets per task, hard no-retry rules, and fallbacks.

item.title: When a premium model is worth it (and when it's just expensive)
item.description: The top-tier model is worth 10x on maybe a tenth of your calls. The trick is knowing which tenth — and it starts with what a wrong answer costs you.

item.title: The boring parts of the AI product are the product
item.description: Your model call is forty lines anyone can write. The moat is the unglamorous machinery around it — and the judgment encoded inside that machinery.

item.title: 5 provider routing mistakes that quietly burn your budget
item.description: None of these show up as errors. They show up as an invoice that's 3–6× what the same traffic should cost, one reasonable-looking call at a time.

item.title: Graceful degradation for AI features
item.description: Every AI feature already degrades. The only question is whether you designed the degraded states or your users are discovering them for you.

item.title: How to evaluate an MCP server before you install it: a 10-point checklist
item.description: Installing an MCP server hands your agent new capabilities and someone else new visibility. Ten checks to run before it touches your config.

item.title: Build vs buy for agent infrastructure
item.description: Your evals are your product. Your retry loop is not. Splitting the agent stack along that line answers the platform question before a vendor call.

item.title: Unit economics for tool calls: budgeting an AI product
item.description: One click becomes forty API calls before anyone looks up. The budgeting discipline that survives that fan-out, worked through with real search rates.

item.title: Local models are underrated infrastructure
item.description: Everyone prices the model ladder from cheap-API up. There's a rung below that: weights on hardware you already own, at a marginal cost of zero.

item.title: Timeouts are a product decision
item.description: Somewhere in your config is a number deciding how long users stare at a spinner for an answer that may never come. Nobody senior chose it.

item.title: Routing tool calls vs routing model calls
item.description: The same ladder idea, two different physics. Why a router that treats search results and model completions identically gets both of them wrong.

item.title: Frugal is the open routing layer for AI tools
item.description: Cost was the wedge. Routing is the product. What's shipping, what changed, and what Frugal Cloud will add.

item.title: Benchmarks lie: evaluate models on your own traffic
item.description: A model's leaderboard position tells you how it does on the leaderboard's distribution, not yours. Fifty queries from your own logs beat it every time.

item.title: Hardening an MCP server's HTTP transport
item.description: The moment an MCP server leaves stdio for HTTP, it becomes a network service with everything that implies. The hardening playbook I actually run.

item.title: Instrumenting an agent: what to log from day one
item.description: Six fields, one JSONL file, first deploy. The instrumentation playbook that answers every question you'll be asked about your agent in month three.

item.title: Token prices fell 90%. Tool prices didn't.
item.description: Inference got an order of magnitude cheaper and everyone noticed. The per-call price of search, scrape, and browse barely moved, and almost nobody did.

item.title: Inside Frugal's router: how a search call picks its provider
item.description: One captured run, walked rung by rung: 0 hits in 529ms, a fall-through, 3 hits at $0, and exactly what lands in the ledger afterward.

item.title: Latency, quality, cost: pick the two your product needs
item.description: Autocomplete, overnight reports, and research tasks live in different corners of the same triangle. Products that pick one corner for everything overpay in all three.

item.title: 5 failure modes every agent tool chain should survive
item.description: Your tool chain will break in exactly five ways. Here's what each one looks like in the logs, and what a chain that survives it does differently.
